item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q009_heme_bundle_fold_not_homology","answer":"No. In SCOPe 2.08, all three groups share the heme-binding four-helical-bundle fold f.21 (SUNID 81344), but SCOPe places them in three separate superfamilies: transmembrane di-heme cytochromes, f.21.1 (SUNID 81342); fumarate-reductase respiratory-complex transmembrane subunits, f.21.2 (SUNID 81343); and respiratory nitrate-reductase 1 gamma chains, f.21.3 (SUNID 103501). SCOPe explicitly says that a fold-level grouping does not imply homology; homology is implied only within each superfamily. The nitrate-reductase annotation notes a possible link and structural similarity to FrdC, but this suggestive observation does not merge the three superfamilies. Likewise, f.21.2 itself contains two families whose bundle is formed by either one chain or two chains. Thus the shared topology and heme-binding architecture may support architecture-level structural comparison, but not cross-superfamily homology, function transfer, residue correspondence, or interchangeable template selection. Any stronger evolutionary or functional claim would require independent sequence, structural-alignment, and preferably phylogenetic/biochemical evidence.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info: /api/v1/, /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__search_scop: discovery searches under /api/v1/releases/2.08/search","mcp__scope__get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81344, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81344/annotations, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81344/homology, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81342, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81342/annotations, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81342/homology, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81343, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81343/annotations, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81343/homology, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/103501, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/103501/annotations, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/103501/homology","mcp__scope__list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81344/children?limit=100"]}]}
